t: Goldman Sachs Highlights Top Tech Stocks With Upside Ahead of Earnings
s: Ahead of the upcoming quarterly results, Goldman Sachs stated that there are numerous top technology companies offering significant investment opportunities and plenty of upside potential. The financial institution highlighted these specific firms this week, advising investors on which leading tech stocks to buy as quarterly earnings reports approach across the sector.

t: Journalist Dom Phillips Warned of Dangers Under Bolsonaro Before Murder
s: Before his tragic death, British journalist Dom Phillips wrote in 2018 that then-candidate Jair Bolsonaro exhibited signs of fascism and would increase dangers for reporters and the Amazon rainforest. Phillips warned that Bolsonaro and his sons represented an extreme threat. The Guardian contributor ultimately paid the ultimate price, highlighting the severe risks faced by those reporting on Brazil's political and environmental landscape during that era.

t: PHP Vulnerabilities Exposed and Exploited Using AI Tools
s: Security researchers utilized artificial intelligence tools to uncover longstanding vulnerabilities in the PHP web scripting language. Following the discovery, attackers began launching AI-assisted exploits against these weaknesses, demonstrating how modern technology can make software bugs significantly more exploitable and highlighting growing cybersecurity concerns regarding automated attacks.

t: AI Discovers PHP2SHELL Vulnerability as Hackers Exploit Leak
s: Artificial intelligence recently discovered a significant security vulnerability known as PHP2SHELL within a foundational part of the internet's architecture. While security researchers scrambled to implement a fix for the newly identified flaw, details regarding the vulnerability unfortunately leaked to the public. Consequently, hackers quickly moved in to exploit the leak, triggering a high-stakes race between security professionals and malicious actors to secure the affected systems.

t: Scientists Vote to Change World Timekeeping Methods
s: Scientists have voted to alter how the world keeps time, though the change will go largely unnoticed by the general public. Philippe Richard, director of Switzerland's Federal Institute of Metrology, discussed the decision in an interview, explaining the reasons behind the adjustment and what it means for official timekeeping standards moving forward.

t: How The Stone Roses' Guitarist Inspired an Introverted Boarding School Student
s: In September 1991, entering a demanding Midlands boarding school where quietness was treated as a weakness, a student found unexpected empowerment. Witnessing John Squire, the guitarist for The Stone Roses, make a vast noise while hiding behind his fringe demonstrated the strength of understatement and the hidden power of being an introvert.

t: STAT Readers Share Perspectives on Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos
s: In recent reader commentary published by STAT, individuals shared their thoughts on various topics, including Elizabeth Holmes and cancer screening. One reader specifically noted that even if Theranos possessed a functioning testing device, the foundational economic model of the company was destined to fail.

t: Earth Entered 'Bad Decades' After Dinosaur-Ending Asteroid Strike
s: A clearer picture has emerged regarding the decades following the massive asteroid impact that caused the extinction of nearly all dinosaurs. New scientific findings detail the severe environmental conditions and ecological disruptions that characterized this tumultuous period on Earth, providing valuable insights into the aftermath of the prehistoric catastrophe and how the planet's ecosystems slowly began to recover from the devastating global event.

t: London Roundhouse hosts star-studded tribute concert for Amy Winehouse's Back to Black
s: Artists including Jorja Smith, Mark Ronson, and Corinne Bailey Rae gathered at London's Roundhouse for a special concert celebrating the 20th anniversary of Amy Winehouse's landmark album, Back to Black. The event, featuring performers close to the late singer alongside the Amy Winehouse Band, was broadcast on BBC Two, offering a reflective tribute to her musical legacy nearly 15 years after her passing.

t: Tango Therapeutics Reports 82% Tumor Response Rate in Advanced Pancreatic Cancer Trial
s: Tango Therapeutics announced that an experimental drug combination achieved an 82% tumor response rate in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer. Revealed ahead of the ESMO conference, the combination therapy builds on recent advancements in treating the disease, demonstrating striking early promise in clinical evaluation for this specific patient population.

t: Wales Plans Consultation on Ban of Steel Pylons for Power Lines
s: The Welsh government has launched a public consultation regarding a new policy that would prioritize underground cables and effectively ban new steel pylons for electricity transmission. The proposed 'undergrounding-first approach' aims to minimize the visual and environmental impact of power infrastructure across the region. Officials are currently seeking views from the public and industry experts on the implementation of this strategy before making any final legislative decisions.

t: Becky Barnicoat Illustrates Scary Halloween Outfits in New Cartoon
s: British publication The Guardian has published a new cartoon by Becky Barnicoat, focusing on scary outfits for the Halloween season. The illustrated piece offers a humorous or artistic take on traditional and frightening costumes associated with the autumn holiday. Readers can view the cartoon directly on the news outlet's website as part of its ongoing creative content.

t: Observing Red Squirrels on Brownsea Island During Autumn
s: An annual autumn trip to Brownsea Island in Dorset offers visitors a prime opportunity to spot red squirrels. Unlike other seasons when the animals remain hidden high in the trees, autumn brings them down to the ground, particularly in the woods behind the church, making it easier for wildlife enthusiasts to observe them up close after taking the ferry from Poole Harbour.

t: NASA Features Andromeda and Rosetta's Selfie in Astronomy Picture of the Day
s: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day featured two distinct cosmic highlights in late October 2026. The daily feature showcases different images and photographs of the universe, accompanied by brief explanations written by professional astronomers. Recent highlights included a view of the Andromeda galaxy titled Andromeda in Southern Spring, and a feature designated as Rosetta's Selfie, continuing the educational series dedicated to exploring the cosmos.

t: Channel 4 Launches New Vertical Social Media Drama Series
s: Channel 4 has released a new vertical social media drama consisting of 90-second episodes, entering the growing global market for short-form mobile content. While vertical dramas are a major phenomenon in countries like China and India, the new five-part release has been described by critics as a slow-release tale lacking traditional dramatic tension.

t: Authors Marlon James and Nicholas Boggs Discuss Life as a Literary Couple
s: Acclaimed novelist Marlon James and biographer Nicholas Boggs, both recognized for their significant literary achievements, discuss their lives and creative work together. As a prominent literary couple, they share insights into how their private and professional worlds intertwine while giving a voice to Black queer history. Both writers serve as mutual critics and witnesses to each other's work, continuing a long tradition of creative partnerships.

t: Phase 3 RISE UP Trial Evaluates Mitapivat for Sickle Cell Disease
s: The global, phase 3, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled RISE UP trial is investigating the efficacy and safety of mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, in patients with sickle cell disease. Affecting over 7 million people worldwide, sickle cell disease causes significant morbidity and mortality, yet access to effective disease-modifying therapies is limited. Mitapivat offers a novel mechanism aimed at ameliorating haemolytic anaemia, potentially providing a new and convenient treatment option for patients.

t: Nature Medicine Publishes Clinical Trial Results for Advanced Melanoma and Bladder Cancer
s: Nature Medicine has published new clinical trial findings presented at the ESMO Congress 2026. The publications detail five-year survival and biomarker analyses from the phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial evaluating relatlimab combined with nivolumab versus nivolumab alone for advanced melanoma. Additionally, results from the phase 2a GDFATHER-NEO trial investigate neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without visugromab in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer, showing encouraging pathological complete response and radiographic outcomes.

t: Paranoia Deepens and Splits Opinion on Celebrity Traitors
s: Paranoia deepens on Celebrity Traitors as traitor behavior splits opinion following a trip to the field of screams. The latest episode revealed the victim of a murder in plain sight ahead of a challenging round table discussion. Additionally, a newly earned special power left a contestant facing a significant decision, leaving the competition on a knife edge.

t: Nvidia CEO Showcases Microduck Robots as 20,000 Units Sell Out
s: During a demonstration, Nvidia's CEO interacted with Microduck robots that respond to voice commands by stomping, making tiny R2D2 noises, sitting, pretending to nap, and doing summersaults. Following the attention, 20,000 units of the interactive toys have successfully sold.

t: Bill Murray Stars in New Golfing Travelogue Series 'A Course Called Ireland'
s: Hollywood star Bill Murray features in a new travelogue series titled 'A Course Called Ireland'. The show follows the actor as he plays golf and engages in pub singalongs, while showcasing his evident fatigue with fame throughout the unconventional and entertaining journey across the country.

t: John Healey pledges budget funding for AI to strengthen UK security
s: British Chancellor John Healey has pledged to use the upcoming budget to commit hundreds of millions of pounds to artificial intelligence. The funding aims to develop a distinctively British approach to AI, designed to bolster the nation's security and prosperity amidst an accelerating global technology arms race, as outlined ahead of his debut budget announcement.

t: Actor Siobhán McSweeney Announced as New Presenter of Guardian Podcast
s: Actor Siobhán McSweeney, known for her role in Derry Girls, has been named as the new presenter of the Guardian’s Comfort Eating podcast. Known for her lifelong love of food, McSweeney recently discussed her culinary preferences and relationship with eating during an interview, featuring items such as crisps, chocolate, and Guinness as she prepares to take over the podcast hosting duties.

t: Anthropic's Early Backers Reportedly Hold Significant Paper Wealth Ahead of Potential IPO
s: Early-stage and follow-on investors in artificial intelligence lab Anthropic are reportedly sitting on major paper returns ahead of a potential initial public offering. Reports indicate that these backers have accumulated substantial unrealized gains based on their investments in the company, highlighting the strong financial positioning of early supporters as the AI startup continues to attract significant attention in the technology sector.

t: USS McFaul Returns to Norfolk After 332-Day Deployment
s: The guided-missile destroyer USS McFaul returned to Naval Station Norfolk, Virginia, on Friday after completing an 11-month deployment. Departing on November 25, 2026, the ship operated independently for 332 days, spending the majority of its time deployed in the Middle East region.

t: GDIT Appoints Amy Johnson as New President
s: General Dynamics Information Technology has named Amy Johnson as its new president. Johnson succeeds Amy Gilliland, who departed the company earlier this month following nearly ten years of leadership at the helm of the business unit.

t: AUKUS Officials Report Progress on Autonomous Undersea Warfare Collaboration
s: AUKUS officials stated that collaboration on autonomous undersea warfare remains on track. During a recent showcase in San Diego, defense technology experts highlighted the capabilities of unmanned underwater vehicles, such as the 34-foot Hadalus-XL developed by Composite Energy Technologies. This large autonomous vehicle is designed to haul several tons of cargo, demonstrating the growing operational value of advanced unmanned systems in modern maritime defense and logistics strategies.

t: Retired Gen. David Petraeus Calls for Urgent U.S. Military Transformation
s: Retired U.S. Army General David Petraeus stated that the American military requires urgent and revolutionary institutional changes to prepare for modern autonomous warfare. While praising the Pentagon's newly established Autonomous Warfare Command, Petraeus emphasized that the United States must rapidly adapt its defense capabilities to meet the demands of contemporary conflict, pointing to the critical need for swift modernization within the armed forces.

t: USS Theodore Roosevelt Participates in U.S.-Japan Exercise Keen Sword 27
s: The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group is operating in the Philippine Sea as part of the joint U.S.-Japan Exercise Keen Sword 27. According to a recent Western Pacific update, the strike group, which includes the cruiser USS Chosin and embarked Carrier Air Wing 11, is leading operations in the region as part of ongoing bilateral military exercises and regional ship movements.

t: Kyiv Explores Purchase of Planned ICEYE and Nokia Communication Satellites
s: Ukraine has signed a letter of intent regarding the potential purchase of planned ICEYE and Nokia sovereign communication satellites. This move follows political tensions and restrictions on Ukraine's access to US Starshield technology, which reportedly impacted military drone operations in the ongoing conflict with Russia. The initiative highlights Kyiv's efforts to secure alternative, independent communication infrastructure for its defense needs during the war.

t: Washington blames Russia for maneuvering military satellite near U.S. spacecraft
s: Washington has accused Moscow of deliberately moving a Russian military satellite close to a U.S.-registered satellite last week. The incident highlights escalating tensions in space, with officials pointing to provocative maneuvers involving an undisclosed mission. The event underscores growing concerns among Western nations regarding security and potential conflicts in Earth's orbit, as rival powers increasingly monitor each other's space assets.
